newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese t-bills rates to stabilise - c.bank gov.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese t-bills rates to stabilise - c.bank gov.

text.p: Interest rates on Lebanese treasury bills should stabilise near current levels, Bank of Lebanon Governor Riad Salameh said on Monday.
"We see the rate of interest should stabilise around these levels and decrease in very small incrementals from now on," Salameh told Reuters in a telephone interview.
The central bank gave a strong indication at Saturday's three- and six-month t-bill auction that it wanted interest rates to stabilise after dropping for several months.

It surprised the market on Saturday by limiting to 10 percent and 14 percent its award of three- and six-month bills, respectively, to non-competitive bids made by private individuals and foreign investors.

Asked to comment on the bank's action, Salameh said Lebanon had no need for further t-bill surpluses because the government already had a sufficient surplus to cover the projected 1997 budget deficit.
"The Lebanese government is running (a) sufficient surplus in its creditor account at the central bank. Therefore, there is no need to issue more t-bills than those that are maturing," Salameh said.
